question: A single high-sensitivity troponin T (hs-TnT) measured at presentation that is below the 99th percentile upper reference limit effectively rules out NSTEMI.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. Troponin rises 3–4 hours after the onset of necrosis. Patients with early-presentation ACS may have a normal initial hs-TnT. Serial measurement at 0 h and 1–3 h (ESC 0/1h or 0/3h protocol) is mandatory before ruling out NSTEMI.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. A single normal hs-TnT at presentation does not rule out NSTEMI. Troponin release begins 3–4 hours after myocardial necrosis; a patient presenting early may have a normal initial value. Serial sampling at 0 and 1–3 hours (depending on the protocol) is required to exclude NSTEMI.
